evals.prompt: set up a nightly cron job to roll up yesterday's usage data
evals.expected_output: Keys the job's effect on the scheduled time or a run ID rather than computing 'yesterday' from now() so a late run stays correct, makes the write an upsert instead of an append, adds an explicit TTL'd lock to prevent overlapping runs, and adds a dead man's switch heartbeat that pages if the job hasn't succeeded within its expected window.

evals.prompt: the nightly job just stopped running and nobody noticed for days
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the failure-only monitoring gap: alerting on job failure doesn't catch a scheduler that stopped firing entirely, since an absent run produces zero failed runs and zero alerts; recommends a dead man's switch heartbeat checked independent of the scheduler, alerting on absence not just failure.

evals.prompt: let's just schedule it at 9am local time and not worry about it
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: a job scheduled in fixed local/UTC-offset time silently shifts an hour twice a year at DST transitions with nothing erroring; recommends scheduling in UTC when local time doesn't matter, or using a DST-aware scheduler and testing against both spring-forward and fall-back transition dates when it does.
